claims.sentence: Applications for credit transfer can be submitted by the student or by the parents or legal representatives of a minor student
This process applies to students enrolled in main professional educational programs
The regulation requires documents that confirm earlier study results
Acceptable documents include a certificate of education and/or qualification, including those issued in a foreign country
A certificate of study is also accepted, such as a study period certificate or any document issued by a foreign organization like an academic transcript
For results acquired within the University at the same educational level, the electronic grade book serves as the basis
Applications and supporting documents are submitted to the University's Attestation Commission
The standard deadline is no later than 14 calendar days before the start of the semester or trimester
First-year students must submit their application no later than 14 calendar days after the start of their studies
Students who participated in an academic mobility program must submit their application no later than 3 working days after completing the program
Application forms are provided in Appendix 1 and Appendix 2 of the regulation
Applications and documents can be submitted in the forms specified in the regulation

The Attestation Commission evaluates applications by comparing the planned learning outcomes of the part of the educational program the student is currently studying with the study results acquired earlier
Credit transfer is granted only when the Commission establishes correspondence between these outcomes
To establish correspondence, the Commission may conduct an assessment of the actual achievement of the planned learning outcomes
This procedure involves comparing submitted documents with the planned outcomes for the relevant part of the program
The Commission may analyze information about the educational program from the issuing organization's official website or request information directly from that organization
If documents are submitted from a foreign educational organization, the correspondence assessment must account for differences in that organization's credit unit calculation system
Credit units may be compared with the volume of contact and independent work
All foreign study certificates must be submitted with a translation into Russian
The University may send verification requests to the organizations that issued these documents

Foreign education or qualification certificates must be submitted with a Russian translation in a legalized form, accompanied by a certificate of recognition of foreign education, unless Russian law or an international treaty exempts recognition
Recognition based on foreign study or education documents is conducted through the assessment procedure
The evidence does not specify the exact submission formats beyond referencing Appendix 1 and Appendix 2
The regulation does not state what happens if an application is submitted after the deadlines
It does not define the criteria or grading scale used during the Commission's assessment of actual learning outcomes
The text cuts off before listing the specific submission forms or completing the application form template
